title: Binary CID keys with Bloom filter are the right choice and should be defended
description: Using cid.to_bytes() as RocksDB keys (36 bytes for CIDv1 raw SHA-256) rather than string encoding is correct: it is compact, avoids codec round-trips, and is the canonical form for IPLD tooling. The Bloom filter on the default column family makes negative lookups cheap, which matters when transit nodes check whether they already have a block before downloading. A future contributor might suggest using the base32-encoded CID string as key for debuggability — resist this: it adds 59 bytes per key and all IPFS tools can decode the binary form anyway.
